page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system utilizes an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs across two threads per core. Cache sizing includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 extensions and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. Memory capacity is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing a substantial 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes a bundled 1,890 GB local NVMe SSD, but does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution metrics paired with balanced multi-threaded throughput. Single-core evaluations place the server in the top tier, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,441.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 3,426.88, and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 39.58 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows strong performance with a PassMark memory score of 2,834.9 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 51.55 GB/sec. Multithreaded synthetic workloads, such as multi-core stress-ng (28,086.9) and Geekbench multi-core (13,544.0), align with expected mid-tier results for a 16 vCPU layout.

The constrained vCPU architecture of the E32-16ads_v7 offers distinct cost efficiency for per-core licensed enterprise software. By allocating 256 GB of memory and fast NVMe storage across 16 vCPUs rather than the standard 32-core allocation for this memory tier, the instance reduces licensing overhead while preserving high memory density. A notable architectural tradeoff is the moderate multi-core throughput, which makes this instance less suited for heavily parallelized batch processing. The hardware profile is optimal for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, and ETL pipelines requiring high memory ceilings and fast local temporary storage.
